resolved_or_reduced: OS NGD Street Address uses the persistent non-null USRN and represents the street providing access to an address rather than an addressable property or parcel
Street Address includes version dates availability windows change type street type classification operational state and operational-state date and requires lifecycle filtering
The earliest documented one-off historic snapshot for Street Address is 2 November 2022 and earlier requests can contain schema inconsistencies
Street features map a USRN to one or more Road Link and Path Link identifiers through explicit cross-reference tables
Street-to-Road-Link and Street-to-Path-Link relationships carry street-version context and can be many-to-many
OS NGD positional accuracy is a semantic quality class rather than a universal numeric accuracy radius
Central Internal and General Internal positions are building-contained address seeds while Postcode Unit and Street Location are coarser contextual positions
Transitional Position can be live before the corresponding topographic feature is captured and Low Accuracy is a priority-review state
Ofcom Spring 2026 used 52 fixed network and 18 fixed wireless access provider submissions for the January 2026 snapshot
Ofcom fixed coverage uses AddressBase Premium and Islands Epoch 123 as the premises base
All Matched Premises requires a match to at least one fixed-provider record with a non-zero predicted download speed while unmatched premises remain unclassified
Decent fixed-or-FWA unavailability explicitly includes unmatched records and zero predicted speeds
Default coverage fields are fixed-line only and FWA is included only where the published field description explicitly mentions WISP or Mobile FWA
Postcode and output-area files suppress full-fibre coverage for commercial confidentiality while retaining gigabit-capable coverage
BDUK struprn is the literal prefix str concatenated with the canonical decimal UPRN to preserve identifier integrity in software
BDUK current_gigabit is a January 2026 OMR plus internal-delivery view and can omit premises delivered after the OMR reference point
BDUK future_gigabit is derived only from OMR responses and can omit non-responding suppliers or contracts agreed after the reference date
BDUK future_gigabit cannot be treated as equivalent to Ofcom planned deployment because the premises bases respondents methods and dates differ
HMLR publication validation checks zero coordinates zero area and duplicate coordinate points
HMLR cleans many self-intersections in the publication environment and removes zero-area polygons and polygons below 0.1 square metres
National Polygon full files can be split at a 2 GB limit and COU contains only the latest version of a changed polygon
